reason: The text fragment (Exodus 2:16-22) describes an encounter at a well in Midian where shepherds (reoim) drive away the daughters of Reuel, a Midianite priest. Moses intervenes and rescues them. The antagonists in this narrative are unnamed shepherds, not identified as Hebrew leaders. The only leader figure presented—Reuel—is actually hospitable and kind, inviting Moses to eat and offering his daughter in marriage. No Hebrew people appear as a group in this text, and no Hebrew leaders are portrayed as antagonistic. The conflict is between shepherds and Midianite women, not between Hebrew leaders and Hebrew people.
